description_html:
The Wildfire-Aware Optimal Transmission Switching (WF_OTS) problem models the operational decisions behind Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS), in which utilities de-energize transmission lines in high-risk areas to reduce the risk of wildfire ignition. Given a wildfire ignition risk for each line, WF_OTS chooses which lines to de-energize so that total load shedding across the network is as small as possible. A small penalty applies to each de-energized line. The total wildfire risk of the lines that stay energized must not exceed a system-wide budget. WF_OTS is a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) under the DC (Bθ) power flow approximation. It has one binary energization variable for each switchable line and continuous variables for generation, line flows, bus voltage angles and load shedding. Big-M constraints enforce the DC power flow equations and the angle-difference limits on energized lines, and relax them on de-energized lines, which carry no power. Each instance is a single operating period (one hour) with fixed wildfire risks, reflecting the short-term operational setting of PSPS decisions.

The MILP formulation for the WF_OTS instances in this library is a single-period version of the Optimal Power Shutoff (OPS) problem [Rhodes21, Piansky25], derived from [Piansky25] and used in [Huang27]. All instances use the California Test System (CATS), a synthetic grid with 8,870 buses, 10,823 branches (661 of them transformers) and 3,892 generators. Line risks come from the daily USGS Wildland Fire Potential Index (WFPI): each line gets the maximum WFPI value of the 1 km pixels it crosses, an integer between 0 and 247. Each instance is one day in 2020–2021, modelled at the hour of that day with the most load shed under threshold-based de-energization. The risk budget equals the risk that remains after de-energizing every line whose risk exceeds the 95th percentile of 2019 risk values, which is 96 in the instances. The instances vary in line risks, bus loads and renewable generator availability [Huang27].

Notation

  • \(\mathcal{N}\): set of buses; \(n^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\mathcal{N}\) is the reference bus.
  • \(\mathcal{G}\): set of generators; \(\mathcal{G}_n\subseteq\mathcal{G}\) are the generators at bus \(n\).
  • \(\mathcal{L}\): set of branches (lines and transformers). Branch \(\ell\) runs from bus \(n_{\ell}^{fr}\) to bus \(n_{\ell}^{to}\). \(\mathcal{L}_n^{fr}\) and \(\mathcal{L}_n^{to}\) are the branches whose from-bus and to-bus is \(n\), respectively.
  • \(\mathcal{L}^{s}\subseteq\mathcal{L}\): switchable lines, i.e., the lines with nonzero wildfire risk on the instance's day. Transformers are never switchable. Its size changes from instance to instance (about 7,900 lines).
  • \(\mathcal{L}^{0}\subseteq\mathcal{L}\): branches with near-zero reactance (\(x_\ell<10^{-4}\) p.u.; 233 branches in CATS). For these branches the instances contain no power-flow equation.
  • \(d_n\): active power demand at bus \(n\) in the modelled hour (p.u., 100 MVA base).
  • \(\overline{p}_i\): available capacity of generator \(i\) in the modelled hour (the hourly renewable availability for renewable units). The generator lower bound is relaxed to 0.
  • \(\overline{f}_\ell\): thermal rating of branch \(\ell\) (p.u.).
  • \(b_\ell = x_\ell/(r_\ell^2+x_\ell^2)\): magnitude of the series susceptance of branch \(\ell\).
  • \(\overline{\delta}=\pi/3\): voltage-angle-difference limit (\(\pm 60^\circ\) on all CATS branches).
  • \(M=2\pi\): big-M constant for angle differences.
  • \(R_\ell\): wildfire risk of line \(\ell\) (an integer WFPI value).
  • \(R^{\mathrm{PSPS}}\): system-wide risk budget, \(R^{\mathrm{PSPS}}=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}:\,R_\ell\le 96} R_\ell\).
  • \(\epsilon=0.01\): penalty per de-energized line.

Variables

  • \(z_\ell\in\{0,1\}\), \(\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}\): 1 if line \(\ell\) stays energized, 0 if it is de-energized.
  • \(p_i\): power output of generator \(i\in\mathcal{G}\).
  • \(f_\ell\in[-\overline{f}_\ell,\overline{f}_\ell]\): active power flow on branch \(\ell\in\mathcal{L}\).
  • \(\theta_n\in[-|\mathcal{N}|\overline{\delta},\,|\mathcal{N}|\overline{\delta}]\): voltage angle at bus \(n\in\mathcal{N}\). These bounds never bind.
  • \(s_n\ge 0\): load shed at bus \(n\in\mathcal{N}\).

MILP formulation

\begin{align} \min\quad & \sum_{n\in\mathcal{N}} s_n \;+\; \epsilon\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}} (1-z_\ell) \\ \text{s.t.}\quad & 0\le p_i\le \overline{p}_i, && \forall i\in\mathcal{G}\\ & 0\le s_n\le d_n, && \forall n\in\mathcal{N}\\ & -\overline{f}_\ell z_\ell\le f_\ell\le \overline{f}_\ell z_\ell, && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}\\ & -\overline{f}_\ell\le f_\ell\le \overline{f}_\ell, && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{s}\\ & -\overline{\delta}-M(1-z_\ell)\le \theta_{n_\ell^{fr}}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to}}\le \overline{\delta}+M(1-z_\ell), && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{0}\\ & -M(1-z_\ell)\le \theta_{n_\ell^{fr}}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to}}\le M(1-z_\ell), && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}\cap\mathcal{L}^{0}\\ & -\overline{\delta}\le \theta_{n_\ell^{fr}}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to}}\le \overline{\delta}, && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}\setminus(\mathcal{L}^{s}\cup\mathcal{L}^{0})\\ & -b_\ell M(1-z_\ell)\le f_\ell-b_\ell(\theta_{n_\ell^{fr}}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to}})\le b_\ell M(1-z_\ell), && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{0}\\ & f_\ell=b_\ell(\theta_{n_\ell^{fr}}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to}}), && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}\setminus(\mathcal{L}^{s}\cup\mathcal{L}^{0})\\ & \theta_{n_\ell^{fr}}=\theta_{n_\ell^{to}}, && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}^{0}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{s}\\ & \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}_n^{fr}} f_\ell-\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}_n^{to}} f_\ell=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{G}_n} p_i-d_n+s_n, && \forall n\in\mathcal{N}\\ & \theta_{n^{\mathrm{ref}}}=0\\ & \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}} R_\ell z_\ell\le R^{\mathrm{PSPS}}\\ & z_\ell\in\{0,1\}, && \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s} \end{align}

The objective minimizes total load shed plus a penalty of \(\epsilon=0.01\) per de-energized line. In the instance files this penalty appears as coefficient \(-0.01\) on each \(z_\ell\) together with a constant \(0.01|\mathcal{L}^{s}|\). The constraints, in order: generator limits; load-shed limits (on buses without load, \(s_n=0\)); flow limits, which force zero flow on de-energized lines; angle-difference limits, relaxed by \(M\) when a line is de-energized (for a switchable branch with near-zero reactance the limit is 0, so the angles at its two ends are equal while it is energized); the big-M DC power flow on switchable lines (the flow big-M is \(b_\ell M=2\pi b_\ell\)); the DC power flow and angle limits on non-switchable branches; nodal power balance with load shedding; the reference angle; and the system-wide wildfire risk budget.

The instance files use the paper's sign convention: [Huang27] writes the flow as \(-b_\ell(\theta_{fr}-\theta_{to})\) with a negative series susceptance, which equals \(b_\ell(\theta_{fr}-\theta_{to})\) with the positive \(b_\ell\) above. Each instance has \(|\mathcal{L}^{s}|\) binary variables, \(|\mathcal{L}|+2|\mathcal{N}|+|\mathcal{G}|\) continuous variables and \(2+2|\mathcal{N}|+4|\mathcal{L}^{s}|+2|\mathcal{L}^{s}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{0}|+3|\mathcal{L}\setminus(\mathcal{L}^{s}\cup\mathcal{L}^{0})|+|\mathcal{L}^{0}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{s}|\) constraints. The average number of binary variables (7,928.94) is not an integer because \(|\mathcal{L}^{s}|\), the number of lines with nonzero risk, changes from day to day.

Medium: ~7,900 (lines with nonzero WFPI risk; varies per instance)
Risk remaining after de-energizing lines with WFPI risk > 96 (95th percentile of 2019 values)

changes: Added notation, variable list and the complete MILP. The formulation was checked against 2 instances, and every constraint family and every count matches.

Prose: added that the DC model is the B-theta model with big-M angle-difference limits; added test system details (CATS, 8,870 buses / 10,823 branches / 3,892 generators), how risk is defined (maximum WFPI pixel on the line) and how the budget is set (95th-percentile threshold of 96), with what varies between instances (risk, loads, renewable availability).

Corrected the sign of the line penalty: the instances use epsilon * sum(1 - z), i.e. a penalty on DE-energized lines (coefficient -0.01 on z plus a constant). [Huang27] Model 1 prints '+eps*sum z', which is a typo; its text and [Piansky25] Eq. (8a) both use (1 - z).

Documented the instance detail that [Huang27] Model 1 leaves out: branches with x < 1e-4 p.u. have no power-flow equation. Non-switchable ones get theta_fr = theta_to instead; switchable ones keep only the flow and angle big-M constraints. Angle-difference limits (+-60 deg) with M = 2*pi follow [Piansky25] Eqs. (8f)-(8h).
Explained why # Var B is not an integer: |L^s| = number of lines with nonzero risk, which varies by day (7,895 and 7,953 in the two instances checked).
Proposed table columns: Test system, # Buses, # Branches, # Generators, # Switchable lines, # Time periods, Risk budget rule.
[Huang27] also has an arXiv version, arXiv:2510.25147 (PSCC 2026), which could be linked.
verification: Fetched WF_OTS/medium/test.csv rows 0 and 1, parsed them with highspy, and grouped rows by variable family and sense.

Row 0: 40,350 variables (7,895 binary z; 32,455 continuous: 10,823 f, 8,870 theta, 8,870 s, 3,892 p) and 73,430 constraints. Row 1: 7,953 binary, 40,408 variables, 73,604 constraints. Both match the count formulas exactly (|L0 cap Ls| = 169 and 171).

Downloaded CATS from GitHub (WISPO-POP/CATS-CaliforniaTestSystem, MATPOWER/CaliforniaTestSystem.m): 8,870 buses, 3,892 generators and 10,823 branches. The instances match it: branch orientation; f bounds = rateA/100; flow coefficients = x/(r^2+x^2) (all taps are 1); angle limits +-60 deg = 1.0472 rad; angle big-M 2*pi (RHS 7.33039 = pi/3 + 2*pi); flow big-M = 2*pi*b_l. All 661 transformers are non-switchable, and the 233 branches without a flow equation are exactly those with x < 1e-4.
Loads are about 0.49-0.57 x CATS Pd (an hourly profile); 2,472 buses carry load. Generator upper bounds are Pmax, 0, or a fraction of Pmax (renewable availability). All generator lower bounds are 0.
Objective: coefficient 1 on s_n (zero-load buses have s_n fixed to 0 by an equality row), -0.01 on every z, and constant 78.95 = 0.01*7,895.
Risk row: integer coefficients between 1 and 130, one for each switchable line. RHS 420,646 (row 0) and 514,366 (row 1) equal exactly the sum of R_l over lines with R_l <= 96 in both instances.
Reference bus: a single equality theta = 0 (bus 1951).
open_questions: The table's # Var C (32,456) is 1 higher than the 32,455 continuous variables in each checked instance. The difference may be the objective constant counted as a variable; this could not be confirmed.
The rule for x < 1e-4 branches (no flow equation, and theta equality only when non-switchable) comes from the instances. The papers do not describe it.
[Huang27] reports 74,933.72 binary variables on average, which is probably a typo for 7,933.72.
